text:
The proposed theater production is titled "The Chorus of Shadows." It reimagines Sophocles’ *Oedipus Rex* by dissolving the fourth wall entirely. Instead of a static stage, the performance takes place in a labyrinthine, multi-room set representing Thebes. Spectators are not passive observers but are assigned roles as citizens, priests, or guards, moving through the space as the narrative unfolds.

The dramatic monologues of Oedipus and the Chorus are delivered in intimate, one-on-one encounters or small group settings, creating intense character-driven moments. However, the plot branches based on audience choices. For instance, when the blind prophet Tiresias appears, the audience must decide whether to believe him or side with Creon, directly influencing which scenes are triggered next. This fusion allows the timeless themes of fate and free will to be experienced viscerally, as the audience’s collective decisions mirror the tragic inevitability of the original text, yet offer a unique, interactive perspective on the ancient story.
